title: Count Good Subarrays
summary: Given an integer array, count the number of subarrays where the bitwise OR of all elements is at least one of the elements in that subarray.
statement: Given an integer array, count the number of subarrays where the bitwise OR of all elements is at least one of the elements in that subarray.
constraints: nums is a nonempty array of nonnegative integers.
A subarray is good when its bitwise OR is equal to at least one element inside that subarray.
hints: For a good subarray, choose a contained element equal to its OR; every other element must have no bit outside that representative.
Use monotonic-style stacks to find how far each value can extend through bitwise subsets, with asymmetric ties so each subarray has one representative.
Multiply valid left and right endpoint choices for every index.
The boundaries exclude the first incompatible value; tie asymmetry prevents duplicate counting when multiple equal representatives occur.
editorial: The boundaries exclude the first incompatible value; tie asymmetry prevents duplicate counting when multiple equal representatives occur.
